Roi.title: What does a late reply cost?

conversion.label: What share of conversations becomes a sale?

Roi.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own inputs, not a sales guarantee.

full.title: Lost-sales calculator
full.intro: See what manual replies cost, using your own numbers. The result updates live and the link is shareable.
full.methodBody: Lost sales = unanswered messages × sale conversion rate × average order value.
assumptions: Unanswered messages = total messages × (1 minus the answered share).
Freed hours assume an average of three minutes per message.
These figures are estimates and don't replace your real business data.

Workload.title: How much of the week goes to repetitive work?
Workload.subtitle: Set four numbers to see how many hours a month are recoverable.

staff.label: How many people do repetitive work?

automatable.label: What share of it can a system take over?

workdays.label: Working days returned to the team

Workload.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own inputs, not a delivery commitment. The automatable share is confirmed after a process review.

full.title: Repetitive-work calculator
full.intro: Use your team's own numbers to see how many working hours go to work a system could do.
full.methodBody: Recoverable hours = people × hours per day × working days × automatable share.
assumptions: A working day is taken as eight hours.
You set the automatable share yourself; the default is a conservative assumption.
This estimate does not replace a review of the actual processes.

Repeat.title: What is your customer data worth?
Repeat.subtitle: Use your own numbers to see what automated reminders bring back each month.

interval.label: How often would they naturally rebuy?

multiple.label: Cost to win a new customer vs. bring one back (estimated)

Repeat.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own inputs, not a sales guarantee. The achievable return rate is deliberately conservative.

full.title: Repeat-customer calculator
full.intro: Your largest revenue source is someone who already bought. See how much of it is unused.
full.methodBody: Recoverable revenue = customers due to rebuy this month × achievable lift in return rate × average purchase.
assumptions: Customers due each month = total customers ÷ rebuy interval.
The achievable lift is held at a conservative 15 percentage points and never pushes the return rate past 100%.
The acquisition-cost ratio is a rounded approximation, not a figure quoted from a specific published source.

Audit.title: What is your online presence out of 100?

questions.hasCustomerDatabase: Do you keep a customer database?
questions.replySpeed: How long does a first reply usually take?
questions.salesChannel: Which route do most sales come through?

Audit.noWins: Nothing significant is missing; the fundamentals are in place.

wins.site: Build a real site; this is the largest gap.
wins.catalog: Put the catalog online so buyers can see without asking.
wins.payment: Add online payment so purchases aren't abandoned halfway.
wins.reply: Cut first-reply time — automated response solves exactly this.
wins.database: Build a customer database so returning them becomes possible.
wins.mobile: Fix the site on mobile; most visits come from there.
wins.contact: Make the contact route obvious on the site.

Audit.disclaimer: This score is an estimate from your answers and a surface-level page check, not a full audit.
Audit.questionnaireOnlyNote: This score is based on your answers alone; no site was checked.
Audit.instagramNote: Instagram pages aren't checked, as automated access isn't possible; we only ask about them.

Terms.title: The framework, before work begins
Terms.banner: This page is a general framework, not a contract; each project gets its own signed agreement.

start.title: How work begins
start.body: Work starts with a short call and a scope document. Delivery begins once both sides agree on that document.

phases.title: Phasing and staged delivery
phases.body: Work ships in defined phases, each with its own usable output. Payment is tied to those same phases.

revisions.title: Revisions
revisions.body: Each phase includes two revision rounds. Further rounds or a scope change are estimated as a new phase.

clientDuties.title: What we need from you
clientDuties.body: Content and images, access to current channels, and one person who can make decisions. Delays on these three move the timeline.

ip.title: IP and code ownership
ip.body: Source, domain, hosting, and every key belong to your organization. No part of the system stays dependent on us.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality
confidentiality.body: Your business and customer data stay confidential. On request, work is published anonymously or not at all.

thirdParty.title: Third-party running costs
thirdParty.body: Servers, domains, AI models, and SMS carry running costs. These are separate from the build fee and the accounts are opened in your organization's name.

support.title: Support scope
support.body: Fixing what we built is free during the warranty period. New features, content changes, and work on other systems fall outside support and are estimated separately.

stop.title: Stopping or withdrawing
stop.body: Either side may stop between phases. Work completed to that point is settled and handed over.

scope.q: Do we have to automate the whole system at once?
scope.a: No. Work starts with one domain — the one with the largest effect. Other domains follow in later phases, based on the result.

prices.q: Why are there no prices on the site?
prices.a: The tools output scope and timing, not a figure. Pricing is set in a short call, against the scope you've defined.

time.a: Work is phased, and the first usable phase is delivered well before the full project completes.

ownership.q: Who owns the code and access?
ownership.a: Your organization: source, domain, hosting, and every key. Nothing stays dependent on us.

iran.q: Does it run reliably from Iran?
iran.a: Yes. Infrastructure, fonts, and tools are chosen to stay fast and reachable from Iran.
